fields.title: Look less, later, or again: place the visual budget at the right stage
fields.thesis: Visual budgets are more than token counts. StackTok selects encoded evidence, PACE allocates input resolution, ViMoD retains recoverable detail, Frames-on-Demand retrieves frames, AdaLoop reprocesses existing state, and OmniKVQuant lowers cache precision. Track whether evidence survives and which costs have already been paid.
fields.axis_0: Before encoding, after encoding, during generation, or at cache storage
fields.axis_1: Discarding, aggregating, keeping external copies, or rereading
fields.axis_2: Question relevance, coverage, generated text, or stopping stability
fields.axis_3: Token count, peak storage, visual loops, or low-bit representations

fields.position: Optimize query relevance while adjusting coverage constraints with budget and switching selection criteria.
fields.tradeoff: Relevance and coverage both matter. Local single-crop selector omits all five paper VLMs and is not a capability comparison.

fields.position: APC previews and adaptively resizes images before encoding; DDAE uses confidence-weighted language and vision attention to extract tokens.
fields.tradeoff: Resizing and post-encoding selection save different stages. The real-checkpoint smoke chiefly covers APC; DDAE has formula/unit-test evidence separately.

fields.position: DART retains coarse and original fine KV; TRACE holds or replaces the detail working set conditioned on causal text state.
fields.tradeoff: Recoverability does not eliminate fine KV memory. Real checkpoints and CUDA gradient diagnostics cover only the models specified in the README.

fields.position: Build caption memory once and revisit relevant frames under a fixed budget when text evidence is insufficient.
fields.tradeoff: Captions can omit details and the gate can fail to reread. Local deterministic caption/query gates do not run a long-video VLM or learned router.

fields.position: Modulate a shared frozen vision block by the question and loop over visual state, spending extra compute on vision.
fields.tradeoff: Loops add processing but no new raw evidence. Full multi-arm training was too costly and was not reproduced; random-token gradients are diagnostic.

fields.position: Set key quantization ranges per short time window and rotate values independently by modality to lower KV precision.
fields.tradeoff: Lower bits are not fewer entries. Local two-bit NumPy reference gives no GPU kernel speed evidence.

fields.title: When token count falls, ask where original details went
fields.body: PACE can remove details by resizing before full encoding. StackTok selects already encoded evidence using question relevance and coverage. ViMoD retains fine KV and can restore a working set mid-generation. Frames-on-Demand keeps revisitable video and a caption index. Recoverability depends on retained evidence and an executable read path.

fields.title: Account separately for active state, peak memory, and extra computation
fields.body: ViMoD's small active set does not erase resident fine KV. OmniKVQuant lowers bytes per entry at some error. AdaLoop adds vision iterations for a more question-specific representation. Token reduction alone omits storage, reread, and iteration overhead.

fields.question: Does a small active ViMoD fine-KV set necessarily use less peak memory than quantized KV?
fields.answer: No. Original fine KV remain for recovery, so active state differs from resident state. Quantization lowers precision but incurs rotation, quantization, and unpacking work. Compare storage tiers, peak memory, and end-to-end latency on matched input; do not multiply working-set fraction and bit width into a claimed result.
fields.example: One book on the desk does not mean the warehouse is empty; compressing each book saves a different resource and still costs retrieval.

fields.question: Do PACE resizing, StackTok selection, and ViMoD rereads lose information at the same point?
fields.answer: APC changes resolution before full encoding; StackTok selects encoded tokens; ViMoD preserves original fine KV. Information lost in low-resolution inputs cannot be recovered merely by later selection. The intervention stage determines both evidence loss and encoding already paid.
fields.example: Small print destroyed during resizing differs from high-resolution detail retained in an inactive cache.

fields.question: Is one extra AdaLoop iteration equivalent to reading another Frames-on-Demand frame?
fields.answer: No. AdaLoop transforms existing state using a question-conditioned shared block. Frame retrieval adds observations. Extra compute need not add evidence, and evidence need not be used correctly. Separate iterations, frames, and stability; gold labels cannot determine serving stops.
fields.example: Reanalyzing a blurry screenshot is not obtaining a clearer frame from the video.

fields.summary: Initial version: compared StackTok, PACE, ViMoD, on-demand frames, visual loops, and KV quantization; screened 16 abstracts and closely read six papers.
